- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast moderately, especially near end of horizon.
- Model often overshoots after a sharp upward spike in sentiment (e.g., +1.00), then corrects downward — apply downward bias in next 3–5 periods.
- Forecast mean reversion is weak in early horizon (1–5 days), but stronger later (10–30 days); adjust for lagged mean reversion in 15+ day forecasts.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in first 3–5 days, model is underestimating momentum — increase forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.25) and price is rising, model underreacts — add 0.5–1.0% upward bias for next 5 days.
- If forecast is flat (±0.1) for 3+ consecutive days and sentiment is positive, model is missing momentum — increase by 0.3–0.7% per day until sentiment shifts.
